text.text: The APF-M1000 was released in 1978 as a second-generation home video game console from APF Electronics. It used cartridge-based games and was designed to compete with systems such as the Atari VCS and Fairchild Channel F. The console used Motorola 6800-based hardware and included a small library of games including Bowling, Baseball, Space Destroyers, and Blackjack. APF later released the Imagination Machine expansion, which combined the console with a computer keyboard and additional hardware.
